title: Greetings and introductions
summary: Say hello, goodbye, and introduce yourself.
content:
## Saying hello

- **Hola**: hi / hello (any time of day)
- **Buenos días**: good morning (until lunch)
- **Buenas tardes**: good afternoon / early evening
- **Buenas noches**: good evening / good night

## Asking how someone is

- **¿Qué tal?**: how's it going? (informal, very common)
- **¿Cómo estás?**: how are you? (informal, *tú*)
- **¿Cómo está usted?**: how are you? (formal)
- **Bien, gracias. ¿Y tú?**: fine, thanks. And you?

## Introducing yourself

- **Me llamo Ana.**: My name is Ana. (literally *I call myself Ana*)
- **Soy Ana.**: I'm Ana.
- **¿Cómo te llamas?**: What's your name? (informal)
- **¿Cómo se llama usted?**: What's your name? (formal)
- **Mucho gusto.** / **Encantado.** (said by a man) / **Encantada.** (said by a woman): nice to meet you.

## Saying goodbye

- **Adiós**: goodbye
- **Hasta luego**: see you later
- **Hasta mañana**: see you tomorrow
- **Nos vemos**: see you

> Remember the upside-down marks: questions start with **¿** and exclamations with **¡**.

quiz.prompt: It is 9 in the morning. You greet your neighbour with:
quiz.explanation: 'Buenos días' is used in the morning, roughly until lunchtime.
'Me llamo Lucía' literally means 'I call myself Lucía'. 'Soy Lucía' also works.

quiz.prompt: A woman is introduced to someone and says 'pleased to meet you'. She says:
quiz.explanation: 'Encantado/a' agrees with the speaker: a woman says 'encantada', a man says 'encantado'.
hints: The ending agrees with the speaker's gender.

quiz.explanation: 'Hasta mañana' means until tomorrow, or see you tomorrow.

quiz.prompt: Which question asks a stranger's name politely (formal)?
quiz.explanation: '¿Cómo se llama usted?' uses the formal 'usted'. '¿Cómo te llamas?' is the informal 'tú' form.
'Bien, gracias' (fine, thanks) is the standard reply. Add '¿y tú?' to ask the question back.

quiz.prompt: You meet your friend's grandmother for the first time. You ask her how she is:
quiz.explanation: With an older person you have just met, use the formal 'usted': '¿Cómo está usted?'. '¿Cómo estás?' is for friends, and '¿Cómo te llamas?' asks her name.
hints: Tú is for friends and family.

quiz.explanation: 'Buenas noches' says both 'good evening' and 'good night'. Noche is feminine, so it is 'buenas', not 'buenos'.

quiz.prompt: Which 'nice to meet you' can anyone say, man or woman?
quiz.explanation: 'Mucho gusto' never changes. 'Encantado' is said by a man and 'encantada' by a woman.
hints: One of them has no -o / -a ending to agree.

listening.text: Buenos días, ¿qué tal?
listening.meaning: Good morning, how's it going?

listening.text: Bien, gracias, ¿y usted?
listening.meaning: Fine, thanks, and you?

listening.meaning: Hello, my name is Marta, nice to meet you.

listening.text: Hola, soy Luis, ¿cómo te llamas?
listening.meaning: Hi, I'm Luis, what's your name?

listening.text: Encantado, soy Pedro, el vecino nuevo.
listening.meaning: Pleased to meet you, I'm Pedro, the new neighbour.
listening.note: New word: el vecino = the neighbour.

listening.text: Buenas tardes, señora, ¿cómo se llama usted?
listening.meaning: Good afternoon, madam, what's your name?

listening.text: Muchas gracias por la ayuda, hasta luego.
listening.meaning: Thanks a lot for the help, see you later.
listening.note: New word: la ayuda = the help.

listening.text: Buenas noches a todos, nos vemos mañana en la clase de español.
listening.meaning: Good night everyone, see you tomorrow in Spanish class.

guide.tip: Spanish questions start with ¿ and exclamations with ¡. Use the accent buttons when you type them.

bites.title: Buenos días, buenas tardes
bites.rule: Día is masculine, so it's buenos días; tardes and noches are feminine, so buenas tardes, buenas noches. They are always plural.

bites.title: Te for friends, se for strangers
bites.rule: ¿Cómo te llamas? goes with tú (friends, kids, classmates); ¿Cómo se llama usted? is the polite version for strangers and elders.

bites.title: Encantado or encantada?
bites.rule: The ending matches the person speaking: a man says encantado, a woman says encantada. Not sure? Mucho gusto works for everyone.
bites.example_meaning: My name is Ana. Pleased to meet you.

bites.title: Questions open twice
bites.rule: Spanish flags a question or exclamation from the start with ¿ and ¡, so you know how to read it before you get there.

sorts.title: Friend or stranger?
sorts.why: Tú forms (estás, te llamas) are for friends; usted forms (está, se llama) are for strangers and elders.

sorts.title: Buenos or buenas?
sorts.why: Día is masculine (buenos días); tarde and noche are feminine (buenas tardes, buenas noches).

sorts.title: Hello or goodbye?
sorts.why: Greetings open a chat; hasta…, adiós and nos vemos close it.

spots.why: Tarde is feminine, so it's buenas tardes.
Día is masculine even though it ends in -a: buenos días.
With tú (llamas) the pronoun is te: ¿cómo te llamas?
With usted the pronoun is se: ¿cómo se llama usted?
Ana is a woman, so she says encantada.
Usted takes the él/ella form: ¿cómo está usted?

builds.meaning: My name is Ana. Nice to meet you.

realm.content:
## En la posada

Every inn in Eldmark opens the same way: a greeting for the time of day, then your name. **Buenas noches, posadera. Me llamo Grok y soy orco.** Guildmates get **¿cómo te llamas?** and a stranger in Highgate gets **¿cómo se llama usted?**.

vocabulary.example_meaning: My name is Grok and I'm an orc.

vocabulary.example_meaning: My guild is called Los Lobos.

meadowbrook.content:
## En la granja

Your first morning on the farm starts with **buenos días** to the hens and **hola** to the neighbours in town. Introduce yourself at the shop with **me llamo…**, thank the shopkeeper with **gracias**, and leave with **hasta mañana**, because tomorrow there is work in the garden.

vocabulary.example: Me llamo Nora y tengo una granja.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My name is Nora and I have a farm.
Nice to meet you, I'm your neighbour.

vocabulary.example: Mi granja está al lado del bosque.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My farm is next to the forest.

rustwake.content:
## Saludos en el páramo

The Dome door opens, and the first thing you need outside is a greeting: **buenos días** to the trader at the market, **hola** to a friendly scavenger. Introduce yourself with **me llamo…**, answer with **mucho gusto**, pay in nuts and say **gracias**, then leave with **hasta luego**. The plains are big.

vocabulary.example_meaning: Good morning, trader. How's it going?

vocabulary.example: Me llamo Dani y soy de la cúpula.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My name is Dani and I'm from the Dome.

vocabulary.example: Mucho gusto, soy Marta, la mercadera.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Nice to meet you, I'm Marta, the trader.

vocabulary.example_meaning: See you later, we'll meet at the market.

vocabulary.example_meaning: Five nuts for a Zafiro soda, thanks.

vocabulary.example_meaning: The plains are big and there's a lot of dust.
